provenance: Sample IATA BCBP (Resolution 792) M1 strings for server/services/bcbp.service.ts.

The three 'encoded' vectors were produced on 2026-11-03 by running encodeBcbpM1 from this repository on the listed inputs, then checked by hand against the BCBP field layout: positions 0-1 format/legs, 2-21 passenger name, 22 E, 23-29 PNR, 30-32/33-35 airports, 36-38 carrier, 39-43 flight number, 44-46 Julian date, 47 compartment, 48-51 seat, 52-56 sequence, 57 status, 58-59 conditional size (hex), then '>' + version 6, section A (0B = 11 chars) and section B (00 or 0D), then '^' + type '1' + hex length + security data.

securityData is HMAC-SHA256 (hex) over base + '\n' + a placeholder pass digest of 64 'd' characters, keyed with the literal secret 'fixture-secret'. Production passes bind to the real pass digest and BOARDING_PASS_SECRET.

The 'iataGuideExample' string is the single-leg example that the bcbp library README reproduces from the IATA BCBP Implementation Guide (DESMARAIS/LUC, YUL-FRA, AC 0834); it is used as an independent decode vector only.
None of these strings has been read by an airport CUSS/CUPPS/gate scanner. Reader acceptance on the target device is an external acceptance step and is not claimed here.

encoded.name: riyadh_new_year
encoded.note: Departure 2026-12-31T22:30Z is 01:30 on 1 January 2027 in Asia/Riyadh, so the Julian date is 001 while the issuance date (UTC 31 Dec 2026) is 6365.

encoded.name: long_name_business_ticket
encoded.note: Surname of 20 letters is cut to 18 so that '/' and one given-name letter fit; hyphen dropped; business maps to compartment J; 13-digit ticket fills section B (airline numeric code + serial).

encoded.name: la_previous_day_child
encoded.note: Departure 2026-01-01T06:30Z is 22:30 on 31 December 2025 in America/Los_Angeles, so the Julian date is 365 of the previous year; flight suffix A kept; child passenger description 3; mobile source M.
